1	# Car Selection Parallel Coordinates Dataset
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	A dataset of 25 car models spanning SUVs, sedans, and electric vehicles, each rated across seven consumer-relevant performance dimensions on a normalized 0–100 scale (higher is better). Designed for multi-dimensional comparison via parallel coordinates.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### cars
     9	- **model** (string): Car model name, 25 unique entries
    10	- **type** (categorical): Vehicle category — one of "SUV" (9 models), "Sedan" (8 models), or "Electric" (8 models)
    11	- **price_score** (integer, 18–88): Affordability score; higher means more affordable
    12	- **fuel_efficiency** (integer, 28–95): Combined fuel/energy efficiency rating
    13	- **power** (integer, 35–95): Engine/motor performance score
    14	- **safety** (integer, 60–92): Composite crash-test and active-safety rating
    15	- **interior_space** (integer, 42–95): Cabin and cargo volume score
    16	- **resale_value** (integer, 35–92): Projected 5-year value retention score
    17	- **emission_rating** (integer, 25–98): Environmental cleanliness score; electric vehicles score near-maximum
    18	
    19	## Data Notes
    20	- All scores are normalized to a 0–100 scale for cross-dimension comparability
    21	- Price score is inverted (higher = more affordable) so that "up" is always "better" on every axis
    22	- Electric vehicles uniformly score 98 on emission_rating, reflecting zero tailpipe emissions
    23	- No single model scores in the top 3 across all seven dimensions simultaneously
    24	- Scores are illustrative estimates based on publicly available consumer review aggregates, not official test results

1	# Mermaid.js Diagram Types
     2	
     3	Comprehensive syntax reference for all 24+ diagram types in Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Core Diagrams
     6	
     7	### Flowchart
     8	Process flows, decision trees, workflows.
     9	
    10	**Syntax:**
    11	```
    12	flowchart {direction}
    13	  {nodeId}[{label}] {arrow} {nodeId}[{label}]
    14	```
    15	
    16	**Directions:** TB/TD (top-bottom), BT, LR (left-right), RL
    17	**Shapes:** `()` round, `[]` rect, `{}` diamond, `{{}}` hexagon, `(())` circle
    18	**Arrows:** `-->` solid, `-.->` dotted, `==>` thick
    19	**Subgraphs:** Group related nodes
    20	
    21	### Sequence Diagram
    22	Actor interactions, API flows, message sequences.
    23	
    24	**Syntax:**
    25	```
    26	sequenceDiagram
    27	  participant A as Actor
    28	  A->>B: Message
    29	  activate B
    30	  B-->>A: Response
    31	  deactivate B
    32	```
    33	
    34	**Arrows:** `->` solid, `->>` arrow, `-->` dotted, `-x` cross, `-)` async
    35	**Features:** Loops, alternatives, parallel, optional, critical regions
    36	
    37	### Class Diagram
    38	OOP structures, inheritance, relationships.
    39	
    40	**Syntax:**
    41	```
    42	classDiagram
    43	  class Animal {
    44	    +String name
    45	    -int age
    46	    +void eat()
    47	  }
    48	  Animal <|-- Dog : inherits
    49	```
    50	
    51	**Visibility:** `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected, `~` package
    52	**Relationships:** `<|--` inheritance, `*--` composition, `o--` aggregation, `-->` association
    53	
    54	### State Diagram
    55	State machines, transitions, workflows.
    56	
    57	**Syntax:**
    58	```
    59	stateDiagram-v2
    60	  [*] --> State1
    61	  State1 --> State2 : transition
    62	  State2 --> [*]
    63	```
    64	
    65	**Features:** Composite states, choice points, forks/joins, concurrency
    66	
    67	### ER Diagram
    68	Database relationships, schemas.
    69	
    70	**Syntax:**
    71	```
    72	erDiagram
    73	  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
    74	  ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
    75	```
    76	
    77	**Cardinality:** `||` one, `|o` zero-one, `}|` one-many, `}o` zero-many
    78	
    79	## Planning Diagrams
    80	
    81	### Gantt Chart
    82	Project timelines, schedules.
    83	
    84	**Syntax:**
    85	```
    86	gantt
    87	  title Project
    88	  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    89	  section Phase1
    90	    Task1 :done, 2024-01-01, 5d
    91	    Task2 :active, after Task1, 3d
    92	```
    93	
    94	**Status:** `done`, `active`, `crit`, `milestone`
    95	
    96	### User Journey
    97	Experience flows, satisfaction tracking.
    98	
    99	**Syntax:**
   100	```
   101	journey
   102	  title User Journey
   103	  section Shopping
   104	    Browse: 5: Customer
   105	    Add to cart: 3: Customer, System
   106	```
   107	
   108	**Scores:** 1-5 satisfaction levels
   109	
   110	### Kanban
   111	Task boards, workflow stages.
   112	
   113	**Syntax:**
   114	```
   115	kanban
   116	  Todo[Task Board]
   117	    task1[Implement API]
   118	    @{ assigned: "Dev1", priority: "High" }
   119	  InProgress[In Progress]
   120	    task2[Fix bug]
   121	```
   122	
   123	### Quadrant Chart
   124	Prioritization, trend analysis.
   125	
   126	**Syntax:**
   127	```
   128	quadrantChart
   129	  x-axis Low --> High
   130	  y-axis Low --> High
   131	  Item A: [0.3, 0.6]
   132	```
   133	
   134	## Architecture Diagrams
   135	
   136	### C4 Diagram
   137	System architecture, components.
   138	
   139	**Syntax:**
   140	```
   141	C4Context
   142	  Person(user, "User")
   143	  System(app, "Application")
   144	  Rel(user, app, "Uses")
   145	```
   146	
   147	### Architecture Diagram
   148	Cloud infrastructure, services.
   149	
   150	**Syntax:**
   151	```
   152	architecture-beta
   153	  service api(server)[API]
   154	  service db(database)[Database]
   155	  api:R --> L:db
   156	```
   157	
   158	**Icons:** cloud, database, disk, internet, server, or iconify.design icons
   159	
   160	### Block Diagram
   161	Module dependencies, networks.
   162	
   163	**Syntax:**
   164	```
   165	block-beta
   166	  columns 3
   167	  a["Block A"] b["Block B"]
   168	  a --> b
   169	```
   170	
   171	**Shapes:** rounded, stadium, cylinder, diamond, trapezoid, hexagon
   172	
   173	## Data Visualization
   174	
   175	### Pie Chart
   176	Proportions, distributions.
   177	
   178	**Syntax:**
   179	```
   180	pie showData
   181	  "Category A" : 45.5
   182	  "Category B" : 30.0
   183	```
   184	
   185	### XY Chart
   186	Trends, comparisons.
   187	
   188	**Syntax:**
   189	```
   190	xychart-beta
   191	  x-axis [jan, feb, mar]
   192	  y-axis "Sales" 0 --> 100
   193	  line [30, 45, 60]
   194	  bar [25, 40, 55]
   195	```
   196	
   197	### Sankey
   198	Flow visualization, resource allocation.
   199	
   200	**Syntax:**
   201	```
   202	sankey-beta
   203	  Source,Target,Value
   204	  A,B,10
   205	  B,C,5
   206	```
   207	
   208	### Radar Chart
   209	Multi-dimensional comparison.
   210	
   211	**Syntax:**
   212	```
   213	radar-beta
   214	  axis Skill1, Skill2, Skill3
   215	  curve Team1{3,4,5}
   216	  curve Team2{4,3,4}
   217	```
   218	
   219	### Treemap

   221	
   222	**Syntax:**
   223	```
   224	treemap-beta
   225	  "Root"
   226	    "Category A"
   227	      "Item 1": 100
   228	      "Item 2": 200
   229	```
   230	
   231	## Technical Diagrams
   232	
   233	### Git Graph
   234	Branching strategies, workflows.
   235	
   236	**Syntax:**
   237	```
   238	gitGraph
   239	  commit
   240	  branch develop
   241	  checkout develop
   242	  commit
   243	  checkout main
   244	  merge develop
   245	```
   246	
   247	### Timeline
   248	Chronological events, milestones.
   249	
   250	**Syntax:**
   251	```
   252	timeline
   253	  2024 : Event A : Event B
   254	  2025 : Event C
   255	```
   256	
   257	### Packet Diagram
   258	Network protocols, structures.
   259	
   260	**Syntax:**
   261	```
   262	packet-beta
   263	  0-15: "Header"
   264	  16-31: "Data"
   265	```
   266	
   267	### ZenUML Sequence
   268	Alternative sequence syntax.
   269	
   270	**Syntax:**
   271	```
   272	zenuml
   273	  A.method() {
   274	    B.process()
   275	    return result
   276	  }
   277	```
   278	
   279	### Mindmap
   280	Brainstorming, hierarchies.
   281	
   282	**Syntax:**
   283	```
   284	mindmap
   285	  root((Central Idea))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate a parallel coordinates chart for car comparison.
Business theme, general public audience.
"""

import json
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

cars = data['cars']['data']
dimensions = data['cars']['dimensions']

# Prepare data structures
types = ['SUV', 'Sedan', 'Electric']
type_colors = {
    'SUV': '#1f4e79',      # Deep business blue
    'Sedan': '#2e8b57',    # Sea green
    'Electric': '#d4a017'  # Muted gold/amber
}

type_light_colors = {
    'SUV': '#aec7e8',
    'Sedan': '#98df8a',
    'Electric': '#ffbb78'
}

# Group cars by type
grouped = {t: [] for t in types}
for car in cars:
    grouped[car['type']].append(car)

# Dimension labels for display (readable names)
dim_labels = {
    'price_score': 'Price\n(Affordability)',
    'fuel_efficiency': 'Fuel\nEfficiency',
    'power': 'Power',
    'safety': 'Safety',
    'interior_space': 'Interior\nSpace',
    'resale_value': 'Resale\nValue',
    'emission_rating': 'Emission\nRating'
}

# Find top performer per axis
top_performers = {}
for dim in dimensions:
    best_car = max(cars, key=lambda c: c[dim])
    top_performers[dim] = best_car['model']

# Create figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 10))
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#ffffff')
ax.set_facecolor('#fafbfc')

# Axis positions
x_positions = list(range(len(dimensions)))

# Draw background bands for each type (subtle behind the lines)
for t in types:
    cars_of_type = grouped[t]
    for car in cars_of_type:
        y_vals = [car[dim] for dim in dimensions]
        ax.plot(x_positions, y_vals, color=type_colors[t], alpha=0.12, linewidth=1.2, zorder=1)

# Draw main lines per car (slightly thicker, more visible)
for t in types:
    cars_of_type = grouped[t]
    for car in cars_of_type:
        y_vals = [car[dim] for dim in dimensions]
        # Highlight top performer cars with thicker lines
        is_top = car['model'] in top_performers.values()
        lw = 2.5 if is_top else 1.6
        alpha = 0.85 if is_top else 0.55
        ax.plot(x_positions, y_vals, color=type_colors[t], alpha=alpha, linewidth=lw, zorder=2)

# Draw top performer markers per axis
for i, dim in enumerate(dimensions):
    best = top_performers[dim]
    for car in cars:
        if car['model'] == best:
            y = car[dim]
            ax.scatter([i], [y], color=type_colors[car['type']], s=180, zorder=5,
                       edgecolors='white', linewidths=2.5)
            # Add small annotation for model name near top markers
            ax.annotate(car['model'], (i, y), textcoords="offset points",
                        xytext=(0, 14), ha='center', va='bottom',
                        fontsize=7.5, fontweight='bold', color=type_colors[car['type']],
                        zorder=6)
            break

# Axis lines and labels
for i, dim in enumerate(dimensions):
    ax.axvline(x=i, color='#cccccc', linewidth=0.8, zorder=0)
    ax.text(i, -8, dim_labels[dim], ha='center', va='top', fontsize=11,
            fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
    # Tick labels
    for tick in [0, 25, 50, 75, 100]:
        ax.text(i, tick, str(tick), ha='center', va='center', fontsize=8,
                color='#777777', alpha=0.9)
        ax.plot([i-0.04, i+0.04], [tick, tick], color='#bbbbbb', linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)

# Set axis limits and remove default spines
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, len(dimensions) - 0.5)
ax.set_ylim(-12, 108)
ax.set_xticks([])
ax.set_yticks([])
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)

# Title and subtitle
ax.set_title('Car Model Comparison Across 7 Consumer Dimensions', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold',
             color='#1a1a1a', pad=20)
ax.text(0.5, 1.02, 'Normalized scores (0–100, higher is better) • Dots mark the top performer on each axis',
        transform=ax.transAxes, ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=11, color='#555555')

# Legend
legend_elements = []
for t in types:
    legend_elements.append(Line2D([0], [0], color=type_colors[t], lw=3, label=t))
legend_elements.append(Line2D([0], [0], color='gray', lw=1.2, alpha=0.5, label='Other models'))
legend_elements.append(Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='gray',
                               markersize=10, markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1.5,
                               label='Top performer per axis'))

ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', frameon=True,
          facecolor='white', edgecolor='#dddddd', fontsize=10, title='Vehicle Type',
          title_fontsize=11)

# Footer note
fig.text(0.5, 0.01, 'Data: 25 car models (SUV, Sedan, Electric) • Scores are illustrative consumer-review estimates',
         ha='center', fontsize=9, color='#999999')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.97])

# Save
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight',
            facecolor='white', edgecolor='none')
plt.close()
print('Saved /app/output/result.png')
